name: Long Straddle
summary: Buy a call and a put at the same strike and expiry; pure long-volatility, direction-agnostic, profits from a large move either way or a vol expansion.

legs.strike_rule: Strike nearest to spot, i.e. the strike whose call delta is closest to 0.50.
Same strike as the call (that is what makes it a straddle).

max_profit: theoretically unlimited on the upside; (strike - 0) * 100 - debit on the downside
max_loss: net debit paid (the full premium of both legs), realized if the underlying finishes exactly at the strike
breakevens: strike + total debit per share (upside) and strike - total debit per share (downside)

greeks.delta: near zero at entry (+/-0.05); becomes strongly directional fast
greeks.gamma: strongly positive -- the largest positive gamma per dollar of any two-leg structure
greeks.theta: strongly negative; an ATM 30-DTE straddle on a $500 underlying bleeds roughly 1.5-2.5% of its premium per day, accelerating toward expiry
greeks.vega: strongly positive, typically +$30 to +$60 per vol point per 1-lot on an index ETF at 30 DTE

typical_dte: 20-60 DTE for vol-expansion trades; 1-7 DTE for event trades; 0DTE only for scheduled macro prints
when_to_use: IV rank <= 25 AND an identifiable catalyst inside the expiry (FOMC, CPI, earnings, FDA date, court ruling). Also valid as a pure vol trade when 30-day IV is below 20-day realized vol by more than 3 vol points, i.e. options are cheap relative to how much the stock is actually moving.
entry_rules: IV rank <= 25 over the trailing 252 days. Buying straddles in high IV is how accounts die.
IV30 < HV20 - 3 vol points (implied cheaper than realized), or a dated catalyst inside the expiry.
Strike = the listed strike closest to spot; |call delta - 0.50| <= 0.05.
Total debit <= 1.5% of equity per position ($750 on $50k). Straddles are expensive; size small.

Required move check: (total debit / spot) must be <= 0.75 * the average absolute move over the last 4 comparable catalysts. If the option market already prices a bigger move than history delivers, skip.
DTE must extend at least 5 calendar days past the catalyst date so you can exit into post-event IV, not expiry.
Both legs OI >= 500, bid/ask <= 8% of mid.
Do NOT enter the day before earnings on a name whose IV rank is above 50 -- you will pay the full vol crush.
Submit both legs as one MLeg order at the combined mid.
management_rules: Take profit: close the whole straddle at +50% of debit, or when either leg alone can be sold for more than the total debit paid.
Vol-crush exit: if the position is held through a scheduled event, close within 30 minutes of the event print regardless of P/L -- IV collapse destroys the straddle even when direction was right.
Stop: close at -40% of debit, or at any point where remaining DTE < 10 and the underlying is within 0.5% of the strike.

Delta drift: if net position delta exceeds +/-0.60 per 1-lot, either take the profit on the winning leg or close the whole thing; a straddle that has become a directional trade is no longer the trade you sized for.
Never hold an ATM straddle inside 7 DTE without a catalyst -- theta becomes brutal.
exit_rules: Hard rule: flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.

No short legs, so there is no assignment risk on this structure. However: ITM long options are AUTO-EXERCISED by the OCC at $0.01 ITM, which would deliver 100 shares per contract. Close both legs before 15:45 ET on expiration day, always. Never rely on a do-not-exercise instruction.
Time stop: close at 7 DTE if the position is not at a profit target and no catalyst remains.

If either leg's bid goes to $0.00 and the other leg is deep ITM, close the ITM leg by limit order and let the worthless leg be abandoned only after confirming it is more than $0.01 OTM at 15:30 ET; otherwise close both.
assignment_risk: No short legs, so no assignment can occur. The exposure is the mirror image: OCC auto-exercise of your own long ITM leg at expiry would create an unwanted 100-share stock position (long from the call, short from the put). Closing by 15:45 ET on expiry eliminates this entirely.
buying_power: Net debit only; both legs are long.
liquidity_needs: ATM strikes are the most liquid on the board, so this is the easiest fill in the family. Still require OI >= 500 and route as a package.
common_mistakes: Buying straddles at high IV rank before earnings and losing on the vol crush despite a correct direction; holding too close to expiry; sizing by contracts instead of debit; forgetting that the breakeven requires a move larger than the market already prices in.
zero_dte_notes: Only justified 5-15 minutes ahead of a scheduled 08:30 or 14:00 ET macro print, and only on SPY/QQQ. 0DTE ATM straddles decay at several percent per hour; without an immediate catalyst this is a guaranteed loser. Compute greeks locally (Alpaca gives none for 0DTE), take profit at +40%, stop at -35%, and never hold past 15:15 ET.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
